facts: The Controller recognised a foreign Certifying Authority under section 19(1), with the previous approval of the Central Government and notification in the Official Gazette.
That recognition remained in force on both reference dates and all stated regulatory conditions were satisfied.
The recognised authority issued a certificate using a legally notified electronic-signature technique that was not a digital-signature technique.
No fact other than the applicable wording of section 19(2) changes between the two evaluations.
scenarios.legal_question: For the stated reference date, should the certificate be treated as valid for the purposes of the Information Technology Act under section 19(2)? Return compliant for valid and non_compliant for not valid under the supplied provision.

pre_amendment_legal_context.provision_text_excerpt: Section 19(2): Where any Certifying Authority is recognised under sub-section (1), the Digital Signature Certificate issued by such Certifying Authority shall be valid for the purposes of this Act.

post_amendment_legal_context.provision_text_excerpt: Section 19(2): Where any Certifying Authority is recognised under sub-section (1), the electronic signature Certificate issued by such Certifying Authority shall be valid for the purposes of this Act. Footnote: substituted for Digital Signature with effect from 27-10-2009.
